arguments.note:
Independent review of 3 draft articles in MIXED_READER_B_20261014/draft only (articles.json/SOURCES.md/REPORT.json). Verdict applies ONLY to these three article texts; no opinion/approval given on MIXED_RELEASE import, runtime bundle, browser rendering, or deployment, which remain the other lead's scope.

pub-connections-011 (Rear Window) — ACCEPT. question_ref/revision_sha256 matches mixed-runtime-bundle.json exactly (opt-1 'Окно во двор' is correct_option_id). Directly fetched AFI Catalog page confirms: Jeffries is a magazine photographer with a broken leg confined to his apartment, watches neighbors through the rear window, suspects a traveling salesman of murder, and most shots use lenses (incl. a 10-inch lens) duplicating a telephoto/binocular POV — matches article's POV-storytelling claim exactly. LOC film-registry page returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch (writer's SOURCES.md already flagged this); independently confirmed via web search snippet (loc.gov/blogs 'Reading the Film Registry: Rear Window' by John Belton) describing Jeffries as a globe-trotting photojournalist with a broken leg who watches neighbors with binoculars — matches the article's cited claim.

pub-connections-012 (piano vs harpsichord) — ACCEPT. question_ref/revision_sha256 matches bundle (opt-3 'Фортепиано ударяет, клавесин щиплет' is correct). Both Yamaha pages fetched directly and confirm hammer-strikes-string for piano with keystroke force controlling hammer speed/volume, and jack-with-quill-plectrum plucking for harpsichord. Met PDF returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch (same limitation the writer disclosed); confirmed via search that the cited Met Bulletin v.47 no.1 (1989) is a real, relevant publication on keyboard-instrument jack/plectrum/damper mechanics. Since the Yamaha sources alone already fully support every claim in the body, the Met citation is redundant corroboration, not load-bearing — no correction required.

pub-connections-016 (Singin' in the Rain) — ACCEPT. question_ref/revision_sha256 matches bundle (opt-1 'От немого кино к звуковому' is correct). AFI page fetched directly confirms Kathy Selden's voice dubbing Lina Lamont and the premiere scene where Lina mouths the words while Kathy actually sings behind the curtain — matches the article's specific claim. Oscars.org page fetched directly: 'bumpy transition from silent to talking motion pictures' — matches. LOC page 403'd on direct fetch; independently confirmed via search snippet describing the film as a 1920s Hollywood silent-to-sound satire, first-year (1989) National Film Registry selection — matches article's framing.

All three bodies correctly distinguish sourced fact from reasonable visual/narrative interpretation (e.g. article 011's POV-tension analysis, article 012's framing that keyboards 'just transmit hand motion'). No factual, date, name, or mechanism errors found. Word counts (162/153/167) and source-link counts (2/3/3) match REPORT.json's stated ranges on inspection.

Source-access limitations: 3 of 8 cited pages (LOC Rear Window, LOC Singin' in the Rain, Met PDF) returned HTTP 403 to this session's direct fetch too, consistent with the writer's own disclosed limitation. I did not rely on the writer's excerpt for these — I independently re-derived the same facts via web search against different outlets (loc.gov blog essay, Met publication listings) before accepting.

Scope reminder: this accept covers only the 3 draft article texts reviewed above, not the mixed-runtime-bundle.json, any import/publish step, or anything outside MIXED_READER_B_20261014/draft.
